rows.verified: Food may be recalled because of pathogen contamination such as Listeria or Salmonella.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency recalls and alerts
rows.verified: Food may be recalled because foreign material such as plastic or metal is present.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency recalls and alerts
rows.verified: Incorrect or missing allergen information can trigger an allergen recall.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency recalls and alerts
rows.verified: Food businesses are responsible for recalling products that are unsafe.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency recalls and alerts
rows.verified: The Food Standards Agency works with local authorities and industry to publish consumer alerts.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency recalls and alerts
rows.verified: Recall notifications explain the risk and the action consumers should take.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency recalls and alerts
rows.verified: Consumers and businesses can subscribe to food and allergy alerts.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency recalls and alerts
rows.verified: The Food Standards Agency may issue safety news when a food risk exists even without a product recall.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency recalls and alerts
rows.verified: Recall action depends on the exact product, batch, date code, hazard, distribution, consumer group and current alert status.

rows.source: Food Standards Agency recalls and alerts
rows.verified: Food-alert evidence is product-, batch- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level food-safety probability.

rows.source: DVSA vehicle recalls and faults
rows.verified: The official recall service checks whether a vehicle, part or accessory has a serious safety recall.

rows.source: DVSA vehicle recalls and faults
rows.verified: Manufacturers normally repair or replace recalled safety-critical items without charging the owner.

rows.source: DVSA vehicle recalls and faults
rows.verified: A vehicle with a serious safety defect should not be driven until the required action is taken.

rows.source: DVSA vehicle recalls and faults
rows.verified: A vehicle registration number can be used to check unresolved safety recalls and MOT history.

rows.source: DVSA vehicle recalls and faults
rows.verified: The service also covers motorcycles, buses, coaches, minibuses, lorries, caravans and horse boxes.

rows.source: DVSA vehicle recalls and faults
rows.verified: Recall checks can cover tyres, child seats, seat belts, harnesses and other components.

rows.source: DVSA vehicle recalls and faults
rows.verified: DVSA records faults that may become unsafe or cause a vehicle, part or accessory to fail legal standards.

rows.source: DVSA vehicle recalls and faults
rows.verified: Vehicle users remain legally responsible for keeping vehicles in a safe condition whenever they are driven.

rows.source: DVSA vehicle recalls and faults
rows.verified: Recall significance depends on the exact vehicle or component, model, year, VIN or registration, defect and repair status.

rows.source: DVSA vehicle recalls and faults
rows.verified: Vehicle-recall evidence is asset- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level road-safety probability.
